question_text: A plate of iron is exposed to a carburizing (carbon-rich) atmosphere on one side and a decarburizing (carbon-deficient) atmosphere on the other side at $700^{\circ}C(1300^{\circ}F)$. If a condition of steady state is achieved, calculate the diffusion flux of carbon through the plate if the concentrations of carbon at positions of 5 and 10 mm ($5 \times 10^{-3}$ and $10^{-2} m$) beneath the carburizing surface are 1.2 and 0.8 $kg/m^3$, respectively. Assume a diffusion coefficient of $3 \times 10^{-11} m^2/s$ at this temperature.The unit of the answer is kg/m^2s.
response:
The flux is positive, indicating carbon diffuses from the carburizing (high-concentration) side toward the decarburizing (low-concentration) side, as expected.

$$\boxed{2.4 \times 10^{-9}}$$
